description: Can PatchAhead read breaking changes out of two versions of a library, with no release note? Each case is a small library before and after an upgrade, read without being imported, and every change a correct reading finds. Several reproduce what real packages did -- requests 2.31 -> 2.32, pydantic 1 -> 2 -- including the readings that went wrong on them at first. A rename read where there is none fails the case even when it is marked as a known gap.

cases.note: The old method survives as a deprecated wrapper whose warning names the new one.
The old name is gone and exactly one new method looks exactly like it.
Same position, same kind, same default, and the names share a word.
A renamed `__init__` parameter is a keyword rename on calls to the class.
`Client` is gone and `StoreClient` has exactly its public methods.
Most libraries define in `_impl` and re-export from `__init__`; the public path is what matters.
Found on pydantic 1 -> 2: a class re-exported from a secondary module disappeared from there but not from where it is defined. Picking the secondary path made the whole class look removed.
Found on pydantic 1 -> 2: `dict` deprecated in favor of `model_dump`, which accepts every argument `dict` did and adds more with defaults. A drop-in, so a rename.
Found on requests 2.31 -> 2.32: `get_connection` deprecated in favor of `get_connection_with_tls_context`, which takes different arguments. Renaming the call would break it.
Found on requests: a deprecated function that calls a helper, without naming any replacement. The helper is not its successor.
Deprecated in both versions: nothing changed in this upgrade.
Found on pydantic 1: `dict()` warned only when `skip_defaults` was passed. That deprecates an argument, not the method.
A method that warns about an insecure option and calls a helper has not been renamed.
Found on pydantic 1 -> 2: `use_proxy` dropped and `slots` added at the same position. Same kind and default, unrelated names: not a rename.

old_files.sdk/__init__.py:
def dataclass(cls=None, *, frozen=False, use_proxy=None):
    return cls

new_files.sdk/__init__.py:
def dataclass(cls=None, *, frozen=False, slots=None):
    return cls

cases.note: Every old keyword is still accepted by **kwargs; nothing breaks.
Two new methods share the removed one's signature; picking either would be a guess.
Same name, new module: a move, which v1 cannot migrate.
Underscored names and private modules are not part of the API a caller depends on.
Callers must now pass a value PatchAhead cannot invent.
The control.

From pandas 2.3 -> 3.0: an internal `BlockManager.to_dict()` went and `to_iter_dict()` came, neither taking anything. A signature with no parameters matches any other, so this was read as a rename -- which would rewrite every `df.to_dict()`. With nothing to compare, it is a removal.

The usual two-step rename, from pandas: 2.1 deprecated `DataFrame.applymap` for `map`, which already existed, and 3.0 removed it. The new version alone shows only a removal; the old one says where it went.
pandas' `DataFrame.applymap` warns 'Use DataFrame.map instead.', while its docstring's See Also names `apply` and `replace` too. The warning is the message to callers and is read first.
